column1: # Queries the catalogue runs that the TraceQL corpus does not contain.
# The corpus at crates/pulsus-traceql/tests/corpus/ is the parser's, and it was
# written to cover the GRAMMAR. Twelve rules of server-implementation.md 3.2 are
# ones no corpus query exercises, so the catalogue's comparison could not tell a
# right rule from a wrong one for them, whatever its agreement count said. Each
# row below is one such rule, with the query that reaches it and what it decides.
# They are counted separately from the corpus's 141 and answered the same way:
# `functional-requirements.md`'s T-C8 state the number in prose, so both move
# when a row is added here.
# each row is answered and compared exactly as the corpus's queries are.

column3: what it decides

a search grouped by an ATTRIBUTE, which 3.2 says is served; the corpus groups only by `name` and `resource.service.name`, both String columns, so no corpus query renders a group key read from the JSON
a group key no span carries: every span groups under `nil` (`docs/api.md` §4.2), one spanset per trace

a group key whose value has the same TEXT at two stored types on one trace — `1` as an integer on one span and `1.0` as a double on another — so a statement that groups on the label alone merges two groups the API keeps apart (`docs/api.md` §4.2: an attribute by-key renders in the arm the sender stored it as)
a trace with more than one group, whose first-appearance order differs from the group values' own order (trace six: `Az` starts before `A\n`)
the SPAN-SCOPED branch of the truthiness rule; the corpus's only truthiness query is unscoped
`| coalesce()` with a group key to drop; the corpus's `| coalesce()` query has no `by()` before it
`topk` over more than one series; the corpus's topk query has one series on this fixture, so the two orders keep the same one
the same, in the other direction
a `span:id` comparison with an id a fixture span HAS; the corpus's three compare a sixteen-character id with a four-character literal, so their answer is empty whichever column the rule reads

a comparison whose selection and baseline are BOTH non-empty, over a resource carried by spans on both sides, with a `topN` small enough that applying it per key and per side differs from applying it once

the other side of the comparison above: its selection carries the spans with events, links and instrumentation attributes, which `compare_both_sides` has only on its baseline — between them the five scopes appear on both sides, so a rule that puts one scope's rows on the wrong side cannot hide in a scope that only ever has one
`with(exemplars=false)`, the one hint that changes a read; no corpus query turns exemplars off
a negated condition that holds on `…05`
presence spelled as a negated absence
an attribute `avg()` over int and double
an aggregate after `by()`, each group its own
two aggregate stages, two entries
`select()` of an event attribute
a `duration` key, Go duration text
a `traceDuration` key
trace order taken before the later filter

the negation of a one-of-two event match
